From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Initial redlines and questions (DPA / SCCs)

Ben —

Thanks for the ping. Quick legal read:

1) Roles: If Greenfield is the controller, Redwood is the processor. We should accept controller-to-processor SCCs but need the DPA to reflect that (explicit role table + operational split). We should not sign any redline that recharacterizes Redwood as a controller for processing related to inference results.

2) SCCs approach: propose using the EU Commission 2021 standard clauses (controller-to-processor) plus an export-addendum (we can supply our template). That will reduce negotiation friction compared to a processor-to-processor conversion.

3) KMS / BYOK: we can offer customer-managed keys for Private deployments. For hosted customers we support a managed KMS with segregation controls; if Greenfield requires HSM-backed BYOK, that will likely need an engineering intake and scope. Ask Jordan to confirm.

4) Evidence: request SOC 2 Type II report (we can provide a redacted report), ISO 27001 snapshot if available, subprocessors list, and a short technical note on transfer mitigations (prefix caching, region routing, KV cache residency).

5) Timing & contingencies: ask Procurement for any mandatory clauses (e.g., liability caps tied to order form value). If they push for modifications to warranty or indemnity, we should route to exec approval.

Ben — if you confirm the planned meeting time, I'll prepare a short legal slide (2 slides) to walk through the redline positions and our suggested compromise language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
